forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Judge override: 0.38 → 0.12. Accumulated evidence across 9 days since last reasoning is uniformly negative. Commercial transits remained at near-zero levels on May 18-19 (5-6/day vs 138 pre-war baseline, USNI News via MarineTraffic AIS). Lloyd's war-risk premium remains approximately 5% of hull value — more than three times the 1.5% threshold required for commercial viability. Maersk, CMA CGM, MSC, and Hapag-Lloyd have all formally suspended scheduled Hormuz transits. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll route (operational since May 18) has been used only by three IRGC-linked Iranian-flagged tankers, excluded from resolution counting per PGSA addendum. Insurance Business reporting confirms physical resumption lags deal signature by weeks even if a deal were reached today. With 21 days remaining to horizon, reaching ≥50 vessels/day for 7 consecutive days requires a 4-step chain (deal signed + insurance reopening + carrier announcements + first vessel departures) — none of which has fired. Iran-US deal probability now at 20%. p=0.12 retains residual tail risk for a surprise diplomatic breakthrough followed by rapid market response.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Lloyd's List Intelligence, USNI News, or MarineTraffic AIS (confirmed by Windward) reports ≥50 daily commercial transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence (primary), USNI News (secondary), MarineTraffic AIS data confirmed by Windward (tertiary). UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report is excluded as lagging confirmation only and does not independently resolve. PGSA self-reported numbers excluded per PGSA addendum.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Lloyd's List/USNI News/MarineTraffic AIS/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit resumption.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption and are a necessary precursor to the 50-vessel threshold.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.20. Three independent negative factors from May 18-20: (1) CNN reported May 20 that US intelligence, based on intercepted Israeli communications and observed military movements, concludes Israel has been preparing a possible strike on Iranian nuclear facilities — a diplomatic complication reported simultaneously with deal-making (S4); (2) Araghchi at the Istanbul Diplomacy Forum on May 19 stated Iran would invoke the JCPOA snapback mechanism if the US maintained military pressure — the first public invocation of snapback in this negotiating round, a hardening of public position (S5); (3) Iran's revised enrichment counter-proposal via Pakistani Interior Minister Naqvi (a shorter moratorium duration, retaining enrichment above 20%) was described as 'insufficient' by a senior US official (Axios, S2). Trump cancelled planned strikes on May 19 citing 'serious negotiations' (S3) but did not name a Witkoff-Araghchi direct meeting. Naqvi's third consecutive day in Tehran indicates mediation continuing but gap not closed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Agreement communicated solely via Pakistani intermediary without direct named principal confirmation by the Trump administration and the Iranian government within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Witkoff or named US principal confirms direct or indirect meeting with Araghchi or named Iranian principal via any confirmed channel (including Pakistani intermediary)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; principal-level engagement via any confirmed channel is necessary for the resolution criteria to be met within the horizon.

Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.

Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support. forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.12. A government-sponsored dissolution bill was co-filed by coalition whip Katz and UTJ's Uri Maklev on May 13, with preliminary Knesset reading scheduled for May 20 (Times of Israel, S6; Haaretz, S7). However: (a) the bill does not include an election date — the election date is set by the Knesset House Committee at least 90 days after final dissolution, not in the bill itself; (b) the bill is at preliminary reading only, requiring committee deliberations and three further Knesset floor readings before becoming law; (c) the resolution criteria for F2 require Netanyahu to personally make a formal announcement naming a pre-Oct-27 election date, or the Knesset to pass a formal dissolution vote — neither of which occurs at preliminary reading. The structural pathway to a resolution-qualifying announcement before EOD June 1, while the bill is still navigating its parliamentary stages, is blocked.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. Netanyahu press conference not on Knesset floor does NOT count — announcement must be a formal Knesset address or publicly filed official government statement naming an election date.

indicators.expected_effect: OBSERVED May 13 (ToI, Haaretz). Dissolution process underway — necessary but not sufficient for F2 resolution before June 1. Three further Knesset readings required; bill does not name election date.

forecasts.question: Will the Israeli Knesset dissolution bill pass its third and final reading — formally dissolving the Knesset and triggering early elections — before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. Dissolution bill co-filed by coalition whip Katz and UTJ's Uri Maklev on May 13 (ToI, S6; Haaretz, S7), with preliminary reading on May 20. Bill has cross-coalition support (Haredi bloc UTJ + Shas co-sponsorship reflects the same factions that reduced the coalition to 60 seats). Three Knesset floor readings and committee deliberations remain. Haredi factions have stated preference for September elections, providing urgency incentive. Netanyahu's blocking capacity is the primary downside risk — PM has historically used dissolution filing as coalition management. p=0.55 reflects genuine cross-coalition legislative alignment but accounts for natural parliamentary process delays and Netanyahu's residual ability to reshape the bill's timeline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset conducts an official roll-call vote on the third reading of the dissolution bill and a majority of MKs vote in favour; OR if knesset.gov.il confirms the bill has passed third reading and dissolution is in effect. A preliminary reading alone does NOT count. Committee approval alone does NOT count. Only final third-reading passage counts.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official website (knesset.gov.il) vote record, confirmed by Reuters AND at least one of: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news. Israeli government press office confirmation also acceptable.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If the bill passes third reading but is immediately challenged at the Supreme Court and a stay is granted within 72h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO until stay is lifted. If the vote is split and Speaker declares a tie or parliamentary procedure dispute: AMBIGUOUS until ruled. If coalition pulls the bill between readings: RESOLVE-NO. If dissolution date set after June 10 but third reading passed before June 10: count as YES (dissolution vote occurred, election date is secondary to this forecast).

indicators.name: Knesset second reading committee approval of dissolution bill
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; committee passage is a necessary precursor to third reading and confirms parliamentary majority has not fragmented.

indicators.name: Haaretz or ToI reports third-reading vote date set by Knesset House Committee
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; scheduling a vote date within the June 10 window confirms parliamentary commitment and eliminates the primary process-delay downside risk.

forecasts.question: Will Israel carry out a confirmed kinetic strike on at least one Iranian nuclear facility (Natanz, Fordow, Isfahan, or Arak — as declared on the IAEA Iranian nuclear programme list) before EOD 2026-06-20?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. CNN reported May 20 that US intelligence, based on intercepted Israeli communications and observed military movements, concludes Israel has been preparing strike packages targeting Iranian nuclear facilities including Natanz and Fordow (S4), cited by three US officials briefed on Israeli planning. IDF Spokesperson did not confirm or deny. Trump administration stated publicly it is unlikely to help Israel carry out such strikes. No satellite-imagery confirmation of pre-positioning available as of May 20. DA caution applied: this CNN intelligence-preparation pattern matches a March 2026 CNN report that did not lead to action within 30 days, and preparation intelligence is chronic rather than determinative. p=0.20 reflects the genuine but non-determinative nature of the preparation reporting, US opposition, and the open Pakistan-mediated diplomatic track.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the IDF, Israeli government, or US DoD publicly confirms an Israeli strike on any IAEA-declared Iranian nuclear facility; OR if the IAEA Director-General issues a public statement confirming physical damage at a declared Iranian nuclear site; OR if satellite imagery analyzed by ≥2 independent OSINT providers (Planet Labs/Maxar/UNOSAT) confirms crater or structural damage at a declared nuclear site. Iranian denial alone does NOT resolve NO — requires independent physical verification or IDF/US DoD statement.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters AND AP/AFP quoting named IDF spokesperson or US DoD official; OR IAEA Director-General public statement; OR Israeli PM/Defense Minister public address naming the target site. OSINT satellite confirmation requires ≥2 independent providers (e.g. Planet Labs/Maxar confirmed by ImageSatIntl and one additional open-source analyst).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes on Iranian military targets outside declared nuclear sites (e.g. IRGC bases, missile depots) = NOT resolved. Cyber attack on nuclear facilities without physical damage = NOT resolved. Strike preparation or sorties that do not reach Iranian territory = NOT resolved. If Iran claims strike occurred but IDF denies and no physical satellite evidence available: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO at horizon.

indicators.name: US-Israel diplomatic consultations reported to break down over strike timing (NYT/Washington Post/Haaretz)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; diplomatic rupture between Washington and Jerusalem over strike authorization historically precedes unilateral Israeli action.

indicators.name: IAEA announces emergency Board of Governors meeting citing credible threat to Iranian nuclear facilities
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; IAEA emergency meetings have preceded or immediately followed kinetic events at declared nuclear sites.
